title: Havasupai Tribe Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: After written notice the Tribal Gaming Office and State Gaming Agency directors meet within ten days, then senior representatives; unresolved disputes go on request to non-binding mediation administered by CPR, and then on demand to binding arbitration before a three-arbitrator panel under CPR rules (last-best-offer format unless opted out, no money damages), with an award final and non-appealable except under 9 U.S.C. 10; the parties keep the right to seek injunctive relief in court, including Arizona Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona.
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended in writing signed by both parties and approved by the Secretary where required, and remains in effect until amended, modified or terminated; appendices may be modified by agreement of the Tribal Gaming Office and State Gaming Agency without amending the compact, and Section 23(b)(3) provides notice 180 days before the first renewal term ends to negotiate a successor compact over a term of up to two years.
renegotiation.locator: SECTION 17. AMENDMENTS; SECTION 3(b)(3) (appendices); SECTION 23. EFFECTIVE DATE AND DURATION, (b)
term.summary: The initial term is the remainder of the term under the Tribe's 2003 compact (if in effect on May 1, 2019) plus ten years, followed by a ten-year first renewal term unless a party gives notice of non-renewal for substantial non-compliance at least 180 days before expiry, and then a final renewal term of up to two years to negotiate a successor.
revenue_sharing.summary: For a tribe other than the five listed large tribes, the Havasupai Tribe contributes 0.75 percent of all Class III Net Win (the higher percentages apply if it exceeds the facility and device limits), 88 percent to the Arizona Benefits Fund and 12 percent to local governments or the Local Communities Fund, in consideration of State exclusivity covenants; Section 11 and Section 12 also cover regulatory cost payments.
sovereign_immunity.summary: Neither the Tribe nor the State waives immunity from third-party claims; the Tribe does not waive immunity by establishing tort procedures but agrees not to assert it within the insurance provisions, and the arbitration section is not a waiver of the State's Tenth or Eleventh Amendment immunity or the Tribe's sovereign immunity.
reviewer: larger model, second pass, whole document
note: First pass cited only the appendix-modification arbitration in Section 3(b)(3) and said the Section 15 main text was cut off; Section 15 in the full text sets out notice, negotiation, mediation, binding CPR arbitration and an injunctive-relief carve-out. First pass said no fixed term; Section 23(b) sets an initial term (remainder of the 2003 compact term plus ten years), a ten-year renewal and a final renewal of up to two years. First pass left revenue null; Section 12 sets percentage contributions of Class III Net Win. The Tribe is not one of the five tribes with the higher tiers unless it exceeds its facility and device limits. Section 12.1 (2021 Compact Trust Fund payments by named contributing tribes) does not bind the Havasupai Tribe. The document is an amended and restated compact approved by letter dated May 21, 2021.

title: Enterprise Rancheria of Maidu Indians of California Secretarial Procedures Amendment
dispute_resolution.summary: Disputes under these Secretarial Procedures begin with a written notice, a written response within 15 days and a meet-and-confer within 30 days; if unresolved either party may seek arbitration before JAMS, but neither party is required to agree to arbitrate, and unresolved disputes may be brought in the federal district court for the district of the Gaming Facility or, if that court lacks jurisdiction, a state court of competent jurisdiction in the county. Sec. 13.4 limits remedies to injunctive relief, specific performance and declaratory relief.
dispute_resolution.locator: SECTION 13.0. DISPUTE RESOLUTION PROVISIONS, Sec. 13.1 Voluntary Resolution; Court Resolution and Sec. 13.2 Arbitration Rules
renegotiation.summary: The procedures may be superseded by a Class III compact agreed by the Tribe and the State (Sec. 15.1), are subject to amendment if the Tribe wishes to engage in other authorized forms of Class III gaming but not within 12 months of the effective date (Sec. 15.2), and written requests to negotiate a new compact are governed by IGRA (Sec. 15.3); Sec. 18.7 Most Favored Nation requires the Secretary to meet and confer on modifying the procedures if the State enters into a more favorable compact with another tribe.
renegotiation.locator: SECTION 15.0. AMENDMENTS; RENEGOTIATIONS, Sec. 15.1 to Sec. 15.3; Sec. 18.7
term.summary: The procedures take effect when signed by the Assistant Secretary-Indian Affairs and are in force for 25 years; if no new compact has been agreed by the termination date they extend automatically for one calendar year unless a superseding compact exists, the Tribe may request a further extension six months before final expiration, and the Tribe may ask the Secretary to withdraw them at any time.
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe pays a pro rata share of the State's regulatory costs into the Special Distribution Fund; Sec. 5.2 requires no Revenue Sharing Trust Fund or Tribal Nation Grant Fund payment during the first seven years of gaming and then 2 percent of Gross Gaming Revenue on Gaming Devices above 350 once more than 350 devices operate.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The State and the Tribe each expressly waive sovereign immunity from suit and enforcement of any judgment or arbitral award, in federal or state court, only for disputes with each other arising under these Secretarial Procedures and limited to injunctive relief, specific performance and declaratory relief (and payment of money expressly required), with no waiver as to third parties.
reviewer: larger model, second pass, whole document
note: These are Secretarial Procedures issued by the Secretary of the Interior, but they contain a full State-Tribe dispute clause (Sec. 13.0) modeled on a compact; the Secretary is not a party to those dispute steps. Sec. 11.x arbitration is the separate County process. This file is the procedures as amended by a 2026 amendment (cover page); compared with the 2016 text, the Sec. 18.7 MFN trigger here also covers Secretarial Procedures, and the sentence making the revenue obligation renegotiable if the County and City agreements lapse is absent. Patron dispute provisions also differ from the 2016 text.

revenue_sharing.summary: Annual payments to the State are a sliding percentage of net win from 1.75 percent to 5 percent, and the Tribe is relieved of them if State law allows certain electronic or Class III games by non-tribal operators or the Wisconsin Constitution is amended to allow other gaming.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The replacement Section XXIV waives sovereign immunity for claims by the State or Tribe to enforce the compact, including collection of money due, while the Tribe may sue State officials for unauthorized activity.
note: Deemed-approved 2003 amendments that replace whole sections and renumber others, so cross-references are hard to follow. The excerpt ends mid-section, and the revenue schedule appears in the renegotiation excerpt as well.

title: Menominee Indian Tribe Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: If the parties have not agreed on proposed terms when the compact term expires, either party may require last best offer arbitration under Section XXIII, and the arbitrator may select only an extension of between 15 and 25 years.
renegotiation.summary: If neither party gives notice of nonrenewal, either party may propose amendments or new terms and the parties must negotiate in good faith, and last best offer arbitration applies if they do not agree by expiration.
term.summary: The compact is extended for 25 years from Federal Register publication of the 2010 amendment, then renews automatically unless either party gives notice of nonrenewal, which the State can serve only after enacting a statute directing it to.
revenue_sharing.summary: Section XXXIII requires an annual payment to the State on June 30 based on net win, and the amendment moves the net-win period to the Tribe's fiscal year ending September 30, while the payment rate is not in the excerpt.
note: Amendment renumbers Section IV.A and VII.A, deletes Section VII.M and XII.D, and replaces Section XXVI. The excerpt ends in the middle of Section XXVI. The Secretary's letter is dated December 22, 2010.

title: Menominee Indian Tribe Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended upon the written agreement of both parties under Section XXXI, and this 2013 amendment was made under that provision.
note: Short amendment that changes one clause, Section VII(A)(6) on financing of gaming facilities, to allow financing by the government of an Indian tribe. The approval letter is dated May 1, 2013.

title: Menominee Indian Tribe Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended upon the written agreement of both parties under Section XXXI, and this 2022 amendment permits event wagering under that provision.
note: 2022 amendments permit event wagering and add an Event Wagering net win definition (Section III.I), but the payment provisions that use net win are not in the excerpt. The certification page has blank date and signature lines.

title: Oneida Tribe of Indians Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: The compact provides for written notice, a meeting of the Governor's and the Nation's representatives within twenty days, optional non-binding mediation, and then arbitration by a three-member panel for the listed articles.
dispute_resolution.locator: XXII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION; XXIII. Negotiation; XXIV. Mediation; XXV. Arbitration
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of both parties, and the State or the Nation may propose regulatory amendments in the thirty days before each fifth anniversary of July 1, 2004, with good faith negotiations and disputes resolved under Article XXII.
renegotiation.locator: XXX. AMENDMENT; XXXII. Periodic Amendment Process, paragraph 1
term.summary: The compact continues in effect until terminated by mutual agreement or by a Nation resolution revoking gaming authority, and it expires April 25, 2102 if the listed provisions are held invalid.
revenue_sharing.summary: The Nation pays the State $20,000,000 installments in 2004 and 2005 and then an annual payment set as a percentage of net win (6% for 2006, 4.5% from 2012), reduced by local government payments up to $1,500,000 a year.
note: Opening is a 2003 Secretary letter (deemed approved) for the Second Amendment. Excerpts contain both the amendment text and the compact's dispute articles, with OCR errors. Section numbers are inconsistent: XXV appears as both the Arbitration and the Duration headings. Arbitration excludes Articles IV, XXIII and XXXII, as printed.

title: Oneida Nation Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of both parties, and the Nation may propose amendments to its event wagering and remote wagering internal control standards at any time, with the State to negotiate in good faith within thirty days.
renegotiation.locator: Recitals (WHEREAS clauses referring to Section XXX); E. Amendment, paragraph 2
note: Third Amendment (executed July 1, 2021), with the Secretary's approval letter dated Aug 16, 2021. It adds event wagering and renumbers Articles XVIII-XXX as XIX-XXXI. The excerpts do not include the compact's dispute, term or payment articles; one passage refers to Article XXIV (formerly XXIII) for good faith negotiation disputes. Text is OCR-garbled in places.

title: Oneida Nation and State of Wisconsin Gaming Compact of 1991 Fourth Amendment
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of both parties, and this Fourth Amendment changes how the annual payment is reduced for payments and in-kind contributions made to Brown and Outagamie County governments.
renegotiation.locator: WHEREAS clauses; paragraph 2 (replacing the fourth paragraph of Article XXXII)
revenue_sharing.summary: The Annual Payment is reduced by payments and fair-market-value in-kind contributions the Nation makes to Brown County, Outagamie County or local governments within them, up to $3,250,000 a year ($3,750,000 when net win exceeds $350,000,000).
note: The two-page amendment changes only one paragraph of Article XXXII. It takes effect on Interior approval or approval by operation of law under 25 C.F.R. 293.12. The definition line reads 'Fomih Amendment', an OCR error for Fourth; the amendment is dated April 24, 2025 in that definition.

title: Red Cliff Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: The compact provides for written notice and a negotiation session within ten days, then non-binding mediation with a mediator, and then arbitration before a single arbitrator if the dispute is not resolved, held at a neutral location.
dispute_resolution.locator: Section XXII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION, subsections C (Negotiation), D (Mediation) and E (Arbitration)
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of the State and the Tribe, and either party may propose regulatory amendments in the thirty days before each fifth anniversary of July 1, 2004, with good faith negotiations; if no agreement is reached, Dispute Resolution applies.
renegotiation.locator: Section XXX. AMENDMENT AND PERIODIC ENHANCEMENT OF COMPACT PROVISIONS, subsections A-C
term.summary: The compact continues until terminated by mutual agreement or by a Tribe ordinance or resolution revoking gaming authority, and the 2003 Amendments take effect on signature and as provided in the Act.
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe pays the State a percentage of annual Class III net win, starting at 1.75% above the first $5,000,000 and rising in tiers of 3% to 5% once net win exceeds $40,000,000, with the first $100,000 retained for Bayfield County under a written agreement.
note: Amendment #2 (2003) to the 1991 compact as amended January 15, 1999. The arbitration 'shall be resolved' wording is marked binding because the excerpt does not state finality expressly, and the arbitration procedure is cut off after paragraph 4. Several sections are repeated in the excerpt.

title: Red Cliff Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact allows the parties to enter into written amendments at any time upon mutual agreement, and this 2010 amendment adds Indian tribal governments to the financing exception in Section VII(A)(6).
renegotiation.locator: WHEREAS clause (referring to Section XXX); amendment of Section VII(A)(6)
note: The Secretary's approval letter (Oct 28, 2010) states the amendment takes effect when notice of approval is published in the Federal Register. The amendment changes only one subsection, VII(A)(6). Signature, date and approval block text is garbled in OCR.

title: Sokaogon Chippewa Community Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: The compact provides for written notice with a response within seven days, a negotiation session within ten days, non-binding mediation with a mediator, and then arbitration before a single arbitrator if the dispute remains unresolved.
dispute_resolution.locator: Section XXII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION, subsections C (Negotiation), D (Mediation) and DI (Arbitration, as printed)
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of both parties, and either party may propose amendments in the thirty days before each fifth or twenty-fifth anniversary of July 1, 2004, with good faith negotiation and disputes resolved under Section XXII.
renegotiation.locator: Section XXX. AMENDMENT AND PERIODIC ENHANCEMENT OF COMPACT PROVISIONS, subsections A-B
term.summary: The compact continues until terminated by mutual agreement or by a Tribe ordinance or resolution revoking gaming authority, with no fixed end date.
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe pays the State an annual percentage of Class III net win, starting at 1.75% of net win above $5,000,000 and rising in tiers up to 5% above $150,000,000, with part of each annual amount retained by the Tribe from 2007 under the printed terms.
note: 2003 Amendments (Amendment #2) to the compact as amended February 20, 1998. The Secretary's letter (Aug 13, 2003) describes the amendment as deemed approved. The excerpts repeat the same passages, and several sections are cut off mid-sentence. The arbitration decision terms beyond the excerpt are not shown.

title: Sokaogon Chippewa Community Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact allows written amendments at any time upon mutual agreement, and this 2013 amendment deletes the Forest and Langlade County limitation from the local government payment provision.
renegotiation.locator: WHEREAS clause (referring to Section XXX); amendment of Section XXXII.A.5
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe retains the first $100,000 of each annual payment for payment to local government(s) with which it has a written agreement, and if there is no such agreement the $100,000 is paid to the State.
note: The Secretary's approval letter (May 27, 2014) approves the amendment. The excerpt includes a 'STATE OF WISCONSIN CONFIDENTIAL DRAFT COMPACT AMENDMENT' footer, and the signature dates are garbled. The amendment changes only one phrase in Section XXXII.A.5.

title: Sokaogon Chippewa Community Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: Under Section XXXVII as printed, a three-member arbitration panel sitting in Madison, Wisconsin, with one arbitrator chosen by the Tribe, one by the Department and one by the other two, decides the dispute, and its decision is final and non-appealable.
dispute_resolution.locator: Section XXXVII, paragraphs 3-4 (arbitration), as printed; cross-reference to Section XXIII (Dispute Resolution)
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of the Tribe and State, and this Third Amendment, executed by both parties as of the last signature date, adds event wagering and technical updates.
renegotiation.locator: Opening recitals of the Third Amendment
note: The Secretary's letter (dated November 2022; the day is garbled) approves the Third Amendment, which renumbers Section XXXVII as XXXVIII for data reporting. The arbitration text appears in two excerpt passages. The printed reference 'XX:111.E' appears to be OCR for a section reference.

title: St. Croix Chippewa Indians Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: The compact provides for written notice and a meeting of the Governor's and Tribe's representatives within twenty days, optional non-binding mediation, and then arbitration by a three-member panel under the compact's rules for the listed articles.
dispute_resolution.locator: Section XXII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION, subsections A (Negotiation), B (Mediation) and C (Arbitration)
renegotiation.summary: The compact may be amended by written agreement of both parties, and either party may propose regulatory amendments in the thirty days before each fifth anniversary of July 1, 2004 (with the Governor for the twenty-fifth anniversary cycle), with good faith negotiations and disputes resolved under Article XXII.
renegotiation.locator: Article XXX, Amendment and Periodic Enhancement of Compact Revisions, subsections A-B
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe pays the State a $3.5 million installment in 2004 and then an annual payment of 4.5% of net win (5% above $200,000,000), reduced by local government payments up to $150,000 a year ($250,000 above $200,000,000 net win).
note: Second Amendment to the 1991 compact (deemed approved, 2003); the text states the compact was amended June 18, 1998. The installment is printed as '$3,500,00' (OCR), and the amount is taken from the words 'Three Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars'. The dispute article text is in the excerpt, but whether the Second Amendment changes it is not clear. Excerpts are cut off mid-sentence.

title: St Croix Chippewa Indians Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact is amended by written agreement of the Tribe and State, and this Third Amendment was executed as of the last signature date and approved by the Secretary.
renegotiation.locator: Opening paragraph of the Third Amendment (unnumbered)
note: The Secretary's letter (April 20, 2022) approves the Third Amendment, which provides for on-reservation remote and retail event wagering. The excerpts show the Compact's definitions, the minimum internal control standards amendment procedure and data reporting changes. A passage refers to disputes resolved under Article XXIII, but the article text is not in the excerpt.

title: Stockbridge Munsee Community Tribal State Gaming Compact
renegotiation.summary: The compact is amended by written agreement of the Tribe and State, and the 2024 Amendment changes definitions, authorized games, wagering accounts, notices, revenue credits and internal control standards.
renegotiation.locator: Amendment preamble, paragraph beginning 'The State of Wisconsin'
revenue_sharing.summary: The Tribe's annual payment to the State is reduced by up to $1 million per tribal fiscal year for listed qualifying expenditures (roads, transportation, law enforcement, fire, emergency medical services and payments to local governments), with excess amounts carried forward.
note: 2024 Amendment to the 1992 compact (as amended 1998, 2003 and 2009). The Secretary's letter (Oct 10, 2024) describes the amendment as deemed approved. The excerpts repeat the same passages several times. The heading 'Section XXIII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION' appears without its text. The base annual payment rate is not in the excerpts.

title: Eastern Shoshone Tribe of the Wind River Reservation Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: The compact provides only that patron gaming disputes are resolved under the Eastern Shoshone Gaming Code, tribal law and regulations; no procedure for disputes between the Tribe and the State appears, and the compact's construction, interpretation and enforcement are governed by Wyoming and federal law.
dispute_resolution.locator: III. C. Resolution of Gaming Disputes; X. RESERVATION OF RIGHTS, D. Interpretation of Compact
renegotiation.summary: The Tribe submits a written request to the State to amend the compact, and any substantive or material amendment requires approval by the Secretary or the NIGC under IGRA.
term.summary: The compact remains in effect twenty years from its effective date, may be extended for any period the Tribe and the State agree, and may end by mutual agreement or by tribal ordinance or resolution revoking Class III gaming authority.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The compact does not waive any immunity of the Tribe except as specifically waived under Section V; the only provision found in Section V on this subject is the Tribe's duty to require its insurer not to decline to indemnify or defend on the basis of sovereign immunity within policy limits.
reviewer: larger model, second pass, whole document
note: Full compact preceded by the Secretary's approval letter. The first pass said the Section V waiver text was not in the excerpt; in the full text Section V is Public Health and Safety and F (Insurance) is the insurer covenant. No State-Tribe dispute procedure and no payment clause (revenue null). Third-party rights clause (Section VIII, numbered 'VII' twice in the text) lets the Tribe, the United States and the State bring enforcement actions.

title: Eastern Shoshone Tribe of the Wind River Reservation Tribal State Gaming Compact
dispute_resolution.summary: For a substantial breach, the compact provides written notice and thirty days to correct before the State or the Tribe may terminate, and it preserves judicial and other remedies available under IGRA.
dispute_resolution.locator: VII. TERM (substantial breach paragraphs); X. RESERVATION OF RIGHTS
renegotiation.summary: The Tribe submits a written request to the State to amend the compact, and amendments that are substantive or material must be approved by the Secretary of the Interior or the NIGC under IGRA.
term.summary: The compact remains in effect until April 19, 2046, may be extended for any period the Tribe and State agree, may be terminated by mutual agreement or a Tribal resolution, and the State may terminate after an uncorrected substantial breach by the Tribe.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The compact states that the Tribe's immunity is not waived except as specifically waived under Section V, and the Section V waiver text is not in the excerpt.
note: Second compact (deemed approved, Secretary's letter dated Aug 2016). The dispute-resolution section of the excerpt is empty; the dispute-related text comes from the term article's breach and remedy paragraphs. The opening letter is badly garbled by OCR. The excerpt ends mid-section.

title: Arapaho Tribe of the Wind River Reservation Secretarial Procedures
dispute_resolution.summary: The procedures provide only that patron gaming disputes are resolved under the Northern Arapaho Gaming Code, tribal law and regulations, with review by a person separate from the initial decider; they set out no dispute procedure between the Tribe and a State, and they give no one other than the Tribe or the United States standing to enforce them.
dispute_resolution.locator: III. OPERATION OF GAMING FACILITIES, C. Resolution of Gaming Disputes; VIII. THIRD-PARTY RIGHTS
renegotiation.summary: The Tribe may request amendments in writing to the Secretary, who may disapprove only on stated grounds, with deemed approval after 45 days to the extent consistent with IGRA; Section IX calls for amendment if expansion or contraction of Class III gaming occurs by law, ruling, or another Wyoming compact.
renegotiation.locator: XI. AMENDMENTS; IX. EXPANSION OR CONTRACTION OF CLASS III GAMING
term.summary: The procedures remain in effect fifteen years from the effective date, may be extended for any period the Tribe and the Secretary agree, and may end by mutual agreement of the Tribe and the Secretary or by tribal ordinance or resolution revoking Class III gaming authority.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The procedures do not waive any immunity of the Tribe; the Tribe must require its insurer not to decline to indemnify or defend on the basis of sovereign immunity within policy limits, subject to stated exceptions.
reviewer: larger model, second pass, whole document
note: These are Secretarial Procedures issued by the Secretary of the Interior after a federal court found the State did not negotiate in good faith and a mediator's selection was rejected by the State; they are not an agreement with the State. No payment or revenue-sharing clause appears (revenue null: the only related text is the Tribe's authority to impose taxes and fees). Dispute clause is limited to patron disputes under tribal law. The first pass flagged immunity as false; the text is a no-waiver reservation plus an insurer covenant, so present is marked true.

title: Arapaho Tribe of the Wind River Reservation Gaming Procedures
renegotiation.summary: The Tribe may request amendments in writing to the Secretary, who may disapprove only on the listed grounds, and an amendment not acted on within 45 days is considered approved to the extent consistent with IGRA.
term.summary: The procedures remain in effect for fifteen years from the effective date, may be extended for any period the Tribe and Secretary agree, and may be terminated by mutual agreement or by a Tribal resolution revoking gaming authority.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The procedures state that nothing in them waives any immunity of the Tribe.
note: Second Amended Class III Gaming Procedures for the Northern Arapaho Tribe, approved by letter dated Aug 2, 2007 (received June 19, 2007). The procedures amend the 2005 Secretarial Procedures. Some signature and approval text is garbled in OCR.

title: Arapaho Tribe of the Wind River Reservation Gaming Procedures
term.summary: The procedures run until December 31, 2040, unless a final NIGC or court order shuts down a Tribe casino, in which case the extension expires 90 days after that order, and they may be extended for other periods the Tribe and Secretary agree.
sovereign_immunity.summary: The procedures state that nothing in them waives any immunity of the Tribe.
note: Third Amended Secretarial Procedures. The Secretary's letter (Oct 3, 2014) extends the term from December 31, 2020 to December 31, 2040 to allow financing secured by gaming revenues. The amendment clause (Section XI) is not in the excerpt.
